analysis_steps.goal: Measure radial velocities from HERMES spectra

method.value: Cross-correlate each spectrum with a carbon-star template mask and fit a Gaussian to the CCF

evidence.quote: The radial velocity (RV) was obtained by cross-correlating the object spectrum with a carbon-star template and fitting a Gaussian function to the mean line profile

key_parameters.value: Mask lines deeper than relative level 0.8, wavelength range 476.9 - 654.7 nm

evidence.quote: All lines with a depth getting below the relative level of 0.8 with respect to the local continuum were kept in the mask.
This mask, covering the wavelength range 476.9 — 654.7 nm

key_parameters.value: 0.07 km/s added in quadrature for long-term stability; 30 spectra near maximum light excluded for shocks

evidence.quote: Thirty spectra were excluded from the orbital analysis because they bear the signature of shocks.

analysis_steps.goal: Disentangle pulsation from orbit with RV only

method.value: Fit asymmetric sine (fixed 530 d) plus Keplerian orbit, subtract pulsation, refit Keplerian by chi-square minimisation

evidence.quote: The RV curve was fitted by a combination of two functions: a Keplerian orbit and an asymmetric sine
the cleaned signal is fitted with a Keplerian orbit alone using a $\chi^2$-minimisation.

key_parameters.value: Keplerian period limited to 6310 +/- 1220 d from the Lomb-Scargle periodogram of the light curve (3 sigma)

evidence.quote: the asymmetric sine period was fixed at 530 d and the Keplerian period was forced to remain in the range 6310$\pm$1220 days.

key_parameters.value: Nine Barnbaum RVs added; extra 0.2 km/s uncertainty on HERMES RVs

evidence.quote: an additional 0.2 $\rm km\,s^{-1}$ uncertainty is added to the RV data from HERMES

assumptions.value: Period imposed from the light curve

evidence.quote: The method allows us to get precise orbital parameters at the price of imposing the period.

fitting.value: chi-square minimisation; parameter errors from square root of covariance diagonal

evidence.quote: The standard deviations of the orbital parameters are obtained by computing the square root of the diagonal elements of the covariance matrix.

validation.value: Compared with the independent ORVARA solution

evidence.quote: another independent method was used on the RV curve cleaned from the pulsation.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit full orbit with RV plus Hipparcos-Gaia astrometry

method.value: ORVARA parallel-tempering MCMC fitting RV, proper motions and parallax simultaneously

evidence.quote: uses a parallel tempering MCMC method to simultaneously fit radial-velocity and astrometric measurements.
We used 15 MCMC temperatures and for each temperature, with 100 walkers run with 5 $\times10^6$ steps per walker.

key_parameters.value: Primary mass Gaussian prior 1.9 +/- 1 Msun; Gaia DR3 parallax prior (434 +/- 21 pc); eccentricity prior e<0.15 added after bimodality

evidence.quote: the primary mass was set as a Gaussian prior of 1.9 $\pm$1 $\rm M_{\odot}$
We therefore re-started the MCMC with an additional prior on the eccentricity ($e<0.15$) to favour the orbital solution with the shorter period

assumptions.value: Companion more massive than V Hya initial mass rejected as inconsistent with its evolutionary stage

evidence.quote: Such a high mass ratio would imply a companion that is more massive than V Hya initial mass, which is inconsistent with its evolutionary stage.

fitting.value: Parallel tempering MCMC; likelihood from RV and astrometric chi-square

evidence.quote: taken as the sum of the $\chi^2$ for the Hipparcos proper motion ($\chi^2_{H}$), the Gaia proper motion ($\chi^2_{G}$), and the long-term Hipparcos-Gaia proper motion ($\chi^2_{HG}$).

validation.value: PSRF convergence test; alternative distance priors; sensitivity test offsetting the Hipparcos mu_alpha point by +4,+2,-2,-4 mas/yr

evidence.quote: The convergence of the chains was assessed by comparing the variance between chains with the variance within each single chain through the potential scale reduction factor (PSRF) estimator

evidence.loc: 3.3 Sensitivity with respect to the Hipparcos data
evidence.quote: We conclude that the obtained orbital parameters are robust against the unreliable $\mu^H_{\alpha*}$ value.

analysis_steps.goal: Test companion nature against the UV excess with an SED

method.value: Superimpose Kurucz A0 spectrum plus 2700 K black body on UV to NIR photometry, reddened by interstellar and circumstellar (amorphous carbon) extinction

evidence.quote: The AGB star was modelled by a black-body of 2700 K (inferred temperature from (cite: Knapp_LC_1999))

key_parameters.value: A0 star 9950 K, radius 1.5 Rsun, mass 2 Msun

evidence.quote: The V Hya B spectrum was modelled as an A0 star with a temperature of 9950 K from Kurucz models

key_parameters.value: Photometric uncertainties set to 2 mag optical, 1 mag NIR

evidence.quote: the uncertainties of the photometric data points have been set to 2 mag in the optical and 1 mag in the near-infrared.

assumptions.value: AV(interstellar) = 0.09 mag; amorphous carbon grains, MNR size distribution a^-3.5, 0.005 to 0.25 micron

evidence.quote: The visual interstellar extinction was estimated to be $A_{V}$ = 0.09 mag
with their radius $a$ distributed following the standard MNR distribution ($dn/da = a^{-3.5}$, with $a_{min}$ = 0.005 $\mu$m and $a_{max}$ = 0.25 $\mu$m

validation.value: The A0 spectrum reproduces the GALEX NUV and FUV points

evidence.quote: reproduces perfectly the GALEX photometric data in the NUV and FUV filters.

analysis_steps.goal: Compare RV signals with the AAVSO light curve

method.value: Remove 17 yr trend from light curve via 530-d rolling mean; plot RV and light curve versus pulsation and orbital phase

evidence.quote: the 17 yr signal was fitted by taking a 530-d rolling mean

analysis_steps.goal: Analyse time variation of Na I, K I, C2 and H-alpha lines

method.value: Plot spectra versus orbital phase and interpolate between phases; compare with a reference carbon star

evidence.quote: the spectra are plotted as a function of the orbital phase and interpolated between the phases to obtain a smooth representation of the variation.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit a conical stellar-jet model to the phase-resolved Na I D1 absorption

method.value: Spatio-kinematic jet model with absorption plus re-scattering source term, fitted to the dynamic Na I spectrum in three steps

evidence.quote: the general fitting procedure is a three-step process: first, the synthetic model spectrum is used to fit the stellar-jet model to the phase-dependent observations and to obtain the best-fitting absorbing jet.

key_parameters.value: Fit over velocity range 0 to -250 km/s; ten free parameters with ranges in Table 3

evidence.quote: to fit V Hya sodium spectral line over the range 0 to -250 $\rm km\,s^{-1}$

key_parameters.value: Template for unattenuated spectrum: X Tra, Doppler-shifted for orbit and modulated at 530 d

evidence.quote: we used the high-resolution spectrum of the carbon star X Tra as template for the unattenuated spectrum.

assumptions.value: Inclination fixed in range from orbital analysis because of strong degeneracy with opening angle

evidence.quote: we constrained the inclination angle

assumptions.value: Blue-shifted emission interpreted as re-scattering of V Hya light

evidence.quote: We interpreted the blue-shifted emission as re-scattering of V Hya light in our line of sight.

fitting.value: MCMC routine as in the cited jet-modelling approach; sampler settings, priors beyond ranges and likelihood not given

evidence.quote: Their modelling approach consists in fitting the model spectral lines created by a parametric jet model to the phase-resolved H$\alpha$ profile using an MCMC routine.

validation.value: Visual comparison of observed and modelled dynamic spectrum

evidence.quote: It can be seen that the model reproduces the temporal modulation of the blue-shifted absorption quite well.

claims.hypothesis: The 17 yr periodic variation of V Hya is due to a binary companion
claims.experiment: HERMES RV monitoring combined with Hipparcos-Gaia astrometry, fitted with a Keplerian plus pulsation model and ORVARA
claims.result: Low-eccentricity orbit with period near 17 yr and inclination about 38 deg
claims.finding: The periodic variation is likely due to orbital motion

evidence.quote: We show that the periodic variation seen for V Hydrae is likely to be due to orbital motion.

claims.hypothesis: The obscuration event and alkaline-line absorption are tied to the companion passage
claims.experiment: Compare RV orbit with AAVSO light curve and Na I and K I line variations versus orbital phase
claims.result: Light-curve minima at superior conjunction; blue-shifted absorption varies with phase
claims.finding: The companion passage across the line of sight correlates with obscuration and blue-shifted absorption

evidence.quote: We correlated the companion passage across the line of sight with the obscuration event and the blue-shifted absorption of alkaline resonant lines.

claims.hypothesis: A conical jet launched from the companion can reproduce the Na I line modulation
claims.experiment: Spatio-kinematic jet model fitted to the phase-resolved Na I D1 dynamic spectrum
claims.result: Best-fit hollow cone with wide opening angle reproduces the modulation of the blue-shifted absorption
claims.finding: A wide conical jet from the companion explains the line variations

evidence.quote: It can be seen that the model reproduces the temporal modulation of the blue-shifted absorption quite well.

claims.hypothesis: The modelled jet orientation matches the large-scale CO bipolar outflow
claims.experiment: Overlay the sky-projected jet axis and line of nodes on ALMA 12CO J=2-1 high-velocity emission
claims.finding: The modelled jet may be the innermost part of the large-scale parabolic structure

evidence.quote: Both geometry and orientation between the two structures match.
the modeled conical jet could be seen as the innermost part of a large-scale parabolic structure.

claims.hypothesis: The companion is a hot main-sequence star able to explain the GALEX UV excess
claims.experiment: SED with A0 Kurucz spectrum plus 2700 K black body for the AGB star, reddened
claims.result: A0 spectrum reproduces the GALEX NUV and FUV photometry
claims.finding: The companion is likely a main-sequence star

evidence.quote: the companion is likely to belong to the main sequence phase.

why_this_method.value: The most generic jet model with fewest free parameters and fewest assumptions about the launch site was chosen

evidence.quote: we choose the most generic model containing the smallest number of free parameters and assumptions about the launching site of the outflow.
The choice of such a modelling tool was motivated by previous large-scale observations of high-velocity outflows

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Simple eclipse by a stellar body rejected; a more extended opaque object attached to the companion is needed

evidence.quote: Due to the particular shape of the eclipse, with a long duration and a deep obscuration, and the system inclination, a simple eclipsing scenario by a stellar body has to be rejected.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Long secondary pulsation and episodic dust condensation considered less likely than the binary

evidence.quote: we consider intrinsic variability scenarios to be less likely to explain the long-term periodicity of the star

limitations_admitted.value: Astrometric orbital parameters are indicative only and the direction of orbital motion is undetermined

evidence.loc: 3.3 Sensitivity with respect to the Hipparcos data
evidence.quote: derived from the astrometry as indicative, rather than precise

limitations_admitted.value: Exact launch site of the jet unknown; no direct evidence of companion motion in the spectrum

evidence.quote: the exact launch site of the jet remains unknown.

referee_caveats_inferred: The ALMA data play only a qualitative overlay role; no ALMA processing or quantitative position-angle comparison is given

Reduced chi-square of 13.65 and 14.0 indicate poor RV fit quality
Jet fit has no stated priors, sampler settings or likelihood, and a fixed inclination
Eccentricity prior e<0.15 was imposed to select the 17 yr solution
